title: Ontario municipal systems that convert housing targets into completed units
question: Which municipal systems can convert housing targets into completed units?
why_it_matters: Provincial targets and housing demand matter only if municipal planning, servicing, approvals, infrastructure, labor, and financing can convert them into occupied homes.
current_support: FTFN has Ontario housing supply progress, CMHC and Statistics Canada data, Toronto application 24 254930 from notice through staff report and Scarborough Community Council recommendation, a dated July 29-31 Council gate with explicit bill-withholding conditions, Toronto's 2025 Development Pipeline, Toronto Water's adopted 2026-2035 capital plan, IESO's 2026 electricity outlook, and Toronto Hydro's OEB distribution proceeding.
missing_evidence: final servicing conditions and detailed design
City Council disposition and enacted by-laws for application 24 254930
satisfaction of the wind-study, land-exchange, and laneway conditions
project-specific infrastructure funding and utility connections
stage conversion and completions by municipality
candidate_records: Toronto application 24 254930 City Council decision and enacted by-laws
next_action: Recheck application 24 254930 after the July 29-31 Council meeting for the disposition, amended recommendations, bill status and enacted by-laws, then track condition compliance, building permits, financing, start, completion, and occupancy.
notes: Phase 55I adds citywide water-capital, provincial electricity, and Toronto distribution-planning layers. The gap remains unresolved because those plans do not prove Council adoption for the selected application, enacted by-laws, condition compliance, project utility connections, a building permit, financing, construction, completion, or occupancy.
